//: AgentTokens: agents authenticate with OIDC access tokens (Entra-first, ADR-0004) and the sample agent then runs a real tool-calling loop over the Anthropic Messages API through this host. CredProx CallerToken keys: Authority = the OIDC issuer whose published metadata validates tokens; Audience = a token minted for any other API is refused; MaxTokenAge = d.HH:mm:ss cap measured from iat. Callers: one entry per agent application; TokenClientIds = the app (client) ids whose tokens (azp claim) map to that caller, verbatim; Operations = NAMED rules — a token is admitted only where its roles claim names the rule, so scopes narrow and never widen. The model route carries the Anthropic key as a StaticKey credential (x-api-key header) held here, never in the agent; the caller's bearer is stripped at authentication and never reaches the provider (journal-proven in the smokes). The meta route is deliberately OUTSIDE the caller's Operations: any token calling it gets 403 before a connection is made — the agent sample shows that refusal as a tool error and carries on. Metering on the model route attributes the provider's usage numbers to the calling agent (M50), through the anthropic usage format named in the route metadata (M54; the value names the format, and a name no reader declares refuses the load). The values below are the real shape — replace the YOUR-* placeholders and the demo key and it runs against Entra plus Anthropic. The offline demo (docker compose + ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development, see README) repoints the issuer, audience, client id and destinations at local stand-ins through appsettings.Development.json.

Metrics.//: Console true prints the CredProx meter to stdout instead of exporting OTLP (the default endpoint OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT). Shorten OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL (ms, default 60000) for demos.
